# Copilot Instructions for gsm.viz

This file provides guidance to AI agents (GitHub Copilot CLI, coding agent, and PR code review) working with code in this repository. `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to this file so Claude Code shares the same instructions.

## Project Overview

**gsm.viz** (v2.4.0) is a web-based JavaScript data-visualization library by Gilead BioStats for clinical trial risk-based monitoring (RBM). It renders interactive charts — scatter plots, bar charts, time series, sparklines, site overviews, and group/country overviews — built on **Chart.js 3** and **D3 7**.

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Language | JavaScript (ES modules) |
| Charting | Chart.js 3, D3 7 |
| Chart.js plugins | chartjs-plugin-annotation, chartjs-plugin-datalabels, @sgratzl/chartjs-chart-boxplot |
| Bundler | esbuild (`src/main.js` → `index.js`) |
| Testing | Jest 29 + jest-environment-jsdom + jest-canvas-mock |
| Transpilation | Babel (preset-env) |
| Formatting | Prettier — single quotes, tab width 4 |
| Deployment | gh-pages |

## Commands

```bash
npm run build          # Bundle + format + test + link bundles (full build)
npm run bundle         # esbuild: src/main.js → index.js (+ sourcemap)
npm test               # Jest test suite
npm run test:coverage  # Jest with coverage report
npm run format         # Prettier: format src, examples, tests
npm run local          # live-server dev server
npm run watch          # esbuild watch mode
npm run deploy         # Deploy examples to gh-pages
```

## Repository Layout

```
src/
├── main.js                → entry point; re-exports all public modules
├── barChart.js            → Bar chart entry
├── barChart/              → Bar chart module internals
├── scatterPlot.js         → Scatter plot entry
├── scatterPlot/           → Scatter plot module internals
├── timeSeries.js          → Time series entry
├── timeSeries/            → Time series module internals
├── sparkline.js           → Sparkline entry
├── sparkline/             → Sparkline module internals
├── groupOverview.js       → Group overview entry
├── groupOverview/         → Group overview module internals
├── data/                  → shared data-handling utilities (SHARED — see scoping)
└── util/                  → shared cross-cutting utilities (SHARED — see scoping)

tests/                     → Jest test files (mirror src/ structure)
examples/                  → HTML demos and docs (not tested by Jest)
index.js                   → GENERATED by esbuild — never edit directly
```

### Module Pattern

Each chart type follows a consistent pattern:

- **Entry file** (`src/<chartType>.js`) — exports the public API
- **Module directory** (`src/<chartType>/`) — contains internal implementation files
- **Data transforms** — pure functions that process input data
- **Config builders** — functions that produce Chart.js or D3 configuration objects
- **Chart renderers** — functions that render charts to canvas/SVG via Chart.js or D3
- **Documentation** — module docs in `examples/docs/` must be updated whenever new functionality, configuration options, mappings, helpers, or public behavior are added to a module

### Chart Modules

| Module | Entry file | Internal directory |
|---|---|---|
| Scatter plot | `src/scatterPlot.js` | `src/scatterPlot/` |
| Bar chart (legacy) | `src/barChart.js` | `src/barChart/` |
| Bars (current) | `src/bars.js` | `src/bars/` |
| Time series | `src/timeSeries.js` | `src/timeSeries/` |
| Sparkline | `src/sparkline.js` | `src/sparkline/` |
| Group overview | `src/groupOverview.js` | `src/groupOverview/` |

### Internal File Roles (present in most modules)

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `checkInputs.js` | Validates and normalizes arguments before rendering |
| `configure.js` | Assembles the full Chart.js / D3 config object |
| `structureData.js` | Pure data transforms — no side effects |
| `getScales.js` | Builds Chart.js axis scale config |
| `getPlugins.js` | Builds Chart.js plugin config (annotations, tooltips, legend, datalabels) |
| `updateData.js` | Applies a data update to an existing chart instance |
| `updateConfig.js` | Applies a config update to an existing chart instance |

## Per-Module Scoping Rules

When reviewing a PR, **limit findings to the modules the PR actually touches**. Do not flag issues in unrelated modules.

### `src/scatterPlot*` · `tests/scatterPlot*`
- Review: data transform correctness in `structureData.js`; scale/axis configuration; tooltip and annotation plugin config; input validation logic.
- Expect tests in: `tests/scatterPlot/`
- Do not flag: behaviour of `barChart`, `timeSeries`, or any other unrelated module.

### `src/barChart*` · `tests/barChart*`
- Review: data structuring and `scriptableOptions` callbacks; annotation and datalabel plugin config; scale setup; input validation.
- Expect tests in: `tests/barChart/`
- Note: `barChart` is the legacy bar implementation. New bar features should go in `bars`.

### `src/bars*` · `tests/bars*`
- Review: spec validation (`validateSpec`, `mergeSpec`); dynamic category logic in `getPlugins/`; data aggregation and axis-swap in `structureData/`; export functionality.
- Expect tests in: `tests/bars/`
- Flag: any change to `defaults.js` that could silently alter existing chart behaviour.

### `src/timeSeries*` · `tests/timeSeries*`
- Review: line/point/distribution data structuring; threshold and interval line logic; scale and plugin (annotation, tooltip, legend, title) config; selected-group update path.
- Expect tests in: `tests/timeSeries/`

### `src/sparkline*` · `tests/sparkline*`
- Review: data structuring and `scriptableOptions`; annotation plugin (value line + thresholds); scale and plugin config; input validation.
- Expect tests in: `tests/sparkline/`

### `src/groupOverview*` · `tests/groupOverview*`
- Review: D3 table construction (`makeTable/`); column definition logic (`defineColumns/`); traffic lighting, sorting, row highlighting, and click events; data structuring and group-metric derivation.
- Expect tests in: `tests/groupOverview/`

### `src/data*` · `tests/data*` — ⚠️ SHARED
- **Elevated scrutiny.** Changes here affect every chart module that imports from `src/data/`.
- Flag: any change to `checkInput.js` or the data schema (`data/schema/`) that could silently break consumers.
- Require: tests that cover all affected data shapes.
- Expect tests in: `tests/data/`

### `src/util*`  — ⚠️ SHARED
- **Elevated scrutiny.** Utilities here are used across multiple modules.
- Flag: behaviour changes to any utility without a corresponding test update.
- Flag: new utility functions added without tests.
- Expect tests in: `tests/util/`
- Note: adding new utilities or modifying existing ones requires explicit discussion (ask-first territory).

### `examples/docs*`
- Flag: a PR that adds new public API, configuration options, or chart behaviour but does **not** update the relevant doc file in `examples/docs/`.

### `.github/workflows*`
- Flag: removal of test or build steps from CI; workflows that do not install dependencies before running tests.

### `index.js`
- **Flag any direct edit as a hard violation.** This file is generated by esbuild from `src/main.js` and must not be edited by hand.

## TDD Compliance (mandatory)

**All code changes MUST follow Red/Green/Refactor TDD. This is a non-negotiable project rule** — every PR that changes implementation code must include a new or updated test.

### The Cycle

```
1. RED    — Write a failing test that describes the expected behavior
2. GREEN  — Write the minimum code to make the test pass
3. REFACTOR — Clean up the implementation while keeping tests green
4. VERIFY — npm test passes, npm run bundle succeeds
5. COMMIT — Save progress with a descriptive message
```

### Rules

- **No implementation code without a failing test first.** Write the test, see it fail, then implement.
- **Bug fixes require reproduction tests.** Write a test that demonstrates the bug (Red), then fix it (Green). This is the Prove-It Pattern.
- Tests live in `tests/<module>/` and mirror `src/` paths.
- Test framework: Jest with jsdom environment and jest-canvas-mock.
- **Flag** any implementation change (new function, modified logic, bug fix) that has no corresponding change in `tests/`.
- **Flag** any removed or skipped test (`test.skip`, `xit`, deleted file) without explanation.
- **Tests are evidence.** "It works" is not sufficient — a passing test suite is required proof. Run `npm test` after every change.

Test distribution target:
- ~80% unit tests on pure functions (data transforms, config builders, utilities)
- ~15% integration tests (rendering pipelines, data pipelines)
- ~5% E2E (full chart render with real data)

### Testing Configuration

- **Jest config:** `jest.config.js`
- **Canvas mock:** `jest-canvas-mock` (setup file, required for Chart.js)
- **Environment:** jsdom (default)
- **Ignored paths:** `/app/`, `/examples/`, `/node_modules/`
- **Test files:** Located in `tests/` directory

---

## Code Conventions

- **ES modules** — use `import`/`export`; no CommonJS `require`.
- **camelCase** for all file names and variable names.
- **Global export:** `gsmViz` (via esbuild `--global-name`)
- **Formatting** — Prettier handles it automatically (single quotes, tab width 4). **Do not flag** whitespace, quote style, or indentation — these are enforced by the formatter on commit.
- **Flag:** mixing `import`/`export` with `require`; PascalCase or snake_case file names; magic numbers or hardcoded strings with no explanatory comment.

```
DEFINE ──→ PLAN ──→ BUILD (TDD) ──→ VERIFY ──→ REVIEW ──→ SHIP

```

## Core Operating Behaviors

These apply at all times, across all tasks:

1. **TDD Always** — Write failing test first, then implement. No exceptions.
2. **Surface Assumptions** — State assumptions explicitly before implementing. Don't silently fill in ambiguous requirements.
3. **Manage Confusion** — Stop when confused. Name the confusion. Ask. Don't guess.
4. **Push Back** — Point out problems directly. Sycophancy is a failure mode.
5. **Enforce Simplicity** — Prefer the boring, obvious solution. If 100 lines suffice, don't write 1000.
6. **Scope Discipline** — Touch only what the task requires. No unsolicited renovation.
7. **Verify with Evidence** — Tests passing, build succeeding. "Seems right" is never done.

## Pull Requests

### Opening a PR

- **Target branch:** Normal feature and fix PRs target `dev` (the default branch). Release PRs target the release commit on `main`.
- Use `gh pr create --base dev` for normal development work or `gh pr create --base main` for a release PR; set the base branch explicitly in the GitHub UI when needed.

### PR Description Structure

```
## Summary

<Short description of what this PR does and why.>

## Changes

- <Bullet list of notable changes>

## Resolved Issues

- Resolves #<issue-number>
- Closes #<issue-number>
```

Include a `Resolves #NNN` or `Closes #NNN` line for every issue this PR addresses so GitHub auto-closes them on merge.

### After Opening

- Monitor Copilot's review comments on the PR.
- Address any meaningful findings (bugs, logic errors, missing tests, security concerns).
- Dismiss or note findings that are style-only or out of scope, but do not silently ignore substantive feedback.

---

## Hard Boundaries — Always Flag

| Violation | Why |
|---|---|
| Direct edit to `index.js` | Generated file — changes will be overwritten by the next build |
| Normal feature or fix PR targets `main` instead of `dev` | Development changes must target the `dev` branch; release PRs are the intentional exception |
| New `npm` dependency added without discussion | Requires team approval; check for prior issue/comment |
| Implementation change with no test | Violates the mandatory TDD rule |
| Failing test removed or permanently skipped | Masks regressions |
| Secrets, credentials, or real patient/clinical data committed | Hard security violation |

## Do Not Flag

- Prettier formatting details (quotes, semicolons, indentation) — the formatter handles it.
- Comment style or quantity — only flag if a comment is actively misleading.
- Variable name micro-choices that are within camelCase convention.
- Changes in `examples/` that are purely cosmetic demo updates with no API impact.

---

## Boundaries

### Always Do

- Write a failing test before implementation (TDD)
- Run `npm test` before commits
- Run `npm run bundle` before commits to keep `index.js` in sync with source (a pre-commit hook enforces this automatically via Husky)
- Follow existing module patterns in `src/`
- Update the relevant module documentation in `examples/docs/` whenever adding new functionality or public behavior
- Use Prettier formatting (single quotes, tab width 4)
- Write descriptive commit messages with type prefixes
- Keep changes small (~100 lines per commit)

### Ask First

- Adding new dependencies
- Changing build configuration (esbuild, Babel)
- Modifying shared utilities (`src/util/`, `src/data/`)
- Changing the Jest configuration
- Creating new chart type modules

### Never Do

- Commit secrets, credentials, or real clinical data
- Edit bundled output (`index.js`) directly
- Remove failing tests without approval
- Skip TDD for any code change
- Push to `main` without review
- Open normal feature or fix PRs targeting `main` directly (release PRs intentionally target `main`)
